title: Shifted Hom continuity for bounded constructible condensed complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and let $E\subseteq\Omega$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X$ be a scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian. Put $E_X=p_X^*C(-,E)$ and work in the ordinary unbounded derived category of internal $E_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ [def-sfb-dcons-subfield]; thus its cohomology is bounded and constructible in the locally finitely presented sense of that definition. Let $I$ be a small filtered category in the module universe, $N:I\to\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Mod}_{E_X})$ a diagram, and $c$ a termwise module-colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose there is an integer $a$ such that $N_i^r=0$ for every $i$ and $r<a$. If $Q$ denotes localization at quasi-isomorphisms, then for every integer $n$ the canonical comparison
$$\varinjlim_{i\in I}\operatorname{Hom}(K,QN_i[n])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(K,Q(c.\mathrm{pt})[n]),\qquad [u_i]\longmapsto Q(c.\iota_i)[n]\circ u_i,$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups. No locally Noetherian hypothesis on $X$, no constructibility of $N_i$, and no colimit universal property in the derived category are assumed.

source.place: Paragraph 2: uniformly bounded-below Hom continuity and finite cone devissage

proof.text: Fix the diagram and cocone in the statement. For an ambient derived object $C$, let $P(C)$ mean that the displayed comparison is an isomorphism for every integer shift, with $K$ replaced by $C$. Apply the general, first part of [det-lem-constructible-ext-continuity-devissage] with $\Lambda=\underline E$, $K_i^\bullet=N_i^\bullet$ and $K^\bullet=c.\mathrm{pt}$. It says that $P$ is closed under shifts, isomorphisms and extensions. This part holds for every scheme; the additional locally Noetherian hypothesis in that node belongs only to its final constructible specialization, which is not used here. The supplied termwise colimit cocone can serve as the colimit in that statement. Equivalently, the universal property gives the unique isomorphism from any chosen termwise colimit to $c.\mathrm{pt}$ commuting with all legs; the isomorphisms in each degree commute with differentials because both composites agree on every colimit leg. Hence this identification preserves precisely the canonical Hom comparison, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Paragraph 2: uniformly bounded-below Hom continuity and finite cone devissage

proof.text: By [def-sfb-dcons-subfield] and [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], each cohomology module $H^q(K)$ is constructible in the specified locally finitely presented ring-object sense, and the cohomology of $K$ vanishes outside a finite interval. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-sheaf-ext-continuity] to $T=X$, the same finite field $E\subseteq\Omega$, $M=H^q(K)$, and the given diagram $N$. Its coefficient ring is exactly $p_X^*C(-,E)=E_X$, and its constructibility condition is exactly the one just specified. Its topological Noetherian and smallness hypotheses hold by assumption; its common termwise lower bound is the given $a$. It concludes $P(H^q(K)[0])$ for every $q$. Neither the cohomology nor the terms of $N_i$ need to be constructible. In particular every shifted cohomology object of $K$ satisfies $P$ by step 1.

source.place: Paragraph 2: uniformly bounded-below Hom continuity and finite cone devissage

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-cohomology-cone-witness] in the abelian category of $E_X$-modules to the bounded object $K$. Obtain its finite list $F_0,\ldots,F_t$ ending in $F_t=K$. Prove $P(F_r)$ by induction on $r$. In the shifted-cohomology alternative this follows from step 2 and invariance under isomorphisms. In the other alternative there are $i,j<r$ and a distinguished triangle $F_i\to F_j\to F_r[s]\to F_i[1]$. Rotate this triangle using (TR2) of [def-weil-triangulated-category], obtaining $F_j\to F_r[s]\to F_i[1]\to F_j[1]$. The induction hypothesis and closure under shifts give $P(F_j)$ and $P(F_i[1])$. The extension closure in the first part of [det-lem-constructible-ext-continuity-devissage] now gives $P(F_r[s])$; shift by $-s$ to get $P(F_r)$. This finite induction establishes $P(K)$. It also covers the zero object, since all its Hom groups are zero.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle (finite cohomology triangles), combined with the finite cone witness and the formal continuity closure

proof.text: Unpack $P(K)$ at the requested integer $n$. Throughout the argument its comparison was induced by the fixed shifted cocone legs, so its value on the class represented by $u_i$ is $Q(c.\iota_i)[n]\circ u_i$. Thus it is the displayed map and is an isomorphism of abelian groups. All colimits used for the targets were termwise module colimits, and the source colimits were in abelian groups.
